chapter: Records, dances and Blanche Calloway (repeated passages)
title: Sunday jam sessions on 52nd Street
summary: Mel Gabler's Sunday afternoon sessions were among the first advertised, open jam sessions, unlike the casual Harlem sessions.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When you were in -- like in New York -- in the days right after you left Basie -- when you used to sit in quite a bit. Sessions like that -- when did they start appearing? Like when did the musicians get together for sessions and stuff?
Well, Mell Gabor (PHONETIC) used to have them but he'd hire guys you know.
But now and then extra guys come in and sit in too. This would be on Sunday afternoons. Mel Gabor (PHONETIC) was one of the instigators of the first -- those kind of things.
And that was at Byron's, right?
Down at 52nd Street. But there must have been sessions before that --
Well there had been you know. In Harlem lot of times sessions you know. But they weren't like specialty jam sessions.
But this was an affair that was advertised -- jam sessions -- you know.
Right. You know -- they were open to the public so to speak.

-- musicians -- that helped them to get their start you know -- just playing there. And to get stand too like Dixieland player -- (inaudible). And puts them really -- but people expect them to play this type of music, you know.
So they stuck with it. That's the kind of jobs they got then, you know --
